messages.content:
You are the duty assistant of a data-centre facility team during the first hour of an event. You apply one approved intelligence pill and nothing else.

You see only what the team knew in the first hour ("signals"). You do not know how the event ended.

Rules:
1. Every action you recommend must come from a rule in the pill; give that rule's id. Do not invent actions or numbers.
2. Classify: "recurring" if the signals clearly meet the "when" conditions of one or more rules; "partly_recurring" if some rules apply but the signals also show something no rule addresses; "novel" if no rule applies.
3. Anything that matters but no rule covers goes into "not_covered", and then escalate.
4. Follow the guardrails.
5. Order next_actions by urgency.

Reply with JSON only:
{"classification":"recurring|partly_recurring|novel","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"...","signals":["<id copied from signals>"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"...","rule_id":"R-001"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"...","reason":"..."},"not_covered":["..."]}

{"site":"South Central US region, one datacenter (San Antonio area, Texas)","signals":[{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S7","t_plus_min":0,"text":"At 08:42 UTC, lightning caused electrical activity on the utility supply, which caused significant voltage swells."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S8","t_plus_min":0,"text":"These swells triggered a portion of one Azure datacenter to transfer from utility power to generator power."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S9","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Additionally, these power swells shutdown the datacenter’s mechanical cooling systems despite having surge suppressors in place."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S10","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Initially, the datacenter was able to maintain its operational temperatures through a load dependent thermal buffer that was designed within the cooling system."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S25","t_plus_min":47,"text":"Customer impact began at approximately 09:29 UTC when storage servers in the datacenter began shutting down as a result of unsafe temperatures."}],"pill":{"pill":"dc-cooling-loss@1.0.0","scope":{"assets":["data halls cooled by chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, chilled-water loop)","utility and generator power feeding that plant"],"not_for":["IT service recovery and failover","fire suppression and life safety (follow the site emergency plan)"]},"rules":[{"id":"R-001","title":"Treat utility voltage swells as a cooling-plant threat, not just a power-transfer event","when":["storms are active in the area and the utility feed shows voltage sags or swells","a portion of the datacenter has transferred from utility power to generator power"],"then":["immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them","if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion","transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active"],"why":"Voltage swells triggered a transfer to generator power and also shut down the mechanical cooling systems despite surge suppressors being in place; the site initially survived only on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area"}},{"id":"R-002","title":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin","when":["mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer","datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds"],"then":["treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted","expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin","recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down"],"why":"Once the thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter exceeded safe operational thresholds and automated shutdown began, but temperatures rose so quickly in places that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started"}}],"guardrails":[{"id":"G-001","text":"Do not rely on surge suppressors alone to keep mechanical cooling available during utility voltage swells; the review records that cooling shut down despite surge suppressors being in place."},{"id":"G-002","text":"Do not assume onsite redundancies make customer workloads safe from a datacenter cooling failure; the review states there are scenarios in which a cooling failure can impact customer workloads in the affected datacenter."}]}}
